meaning: Wording differs, clinical content identical.
Register or word order changed, no clinical fact changed.
A clinical fact changed (number, negation, drug or disease, dropped clause, changed option).
The Bangla supports a different option than the answer key.
Natural Bangla. Nothing marks it as translated.
Slightly stiff or over-formal, but correct. A native speaker would not stumble.
Clearly translated. Word order or phrasing follows the English. Still understood on one reading.
Hard to read. It needs a second pass, or a sentence has to be guessed at.
Not usable Bangla. Broken grammar, wrong script, or English in place of Bangla.
Whether the item is acceptable as it is.
A number, dose, lab value, unit, age, sex, side or duration is missing, changed or misplaced.
A negative was dropped or added. No fever becomes fever.
A drug or condition name became a different drug or condition.
A clinical clause in the English is missing from the Bangla.
An option now reads like a different option, or points at a different answer.
The meaning changed in a way no other tag covers. Describe it in the note column.
English left in the Bangla outside parentheses.
The English term added in parentheses after the Bangla term.
Letters from another script, or a visible encoding defect.
The Bangla has fewer options than the English.
Rate fluency with the English out of view. Then read the English, then set the tier and the tags.
Separate several tags with a semicolon, for example number;clause_dropped. Leave empty when nothing applies.
